newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Foreign doctors monitor Yeltsin's surgery.
newsitem.headline: Foreign doctors monitor Yeltsin's surgery.

text.p: Two groups of foreign doctors arrived at Moscow's Cardiology Research Centre on Tuesday to monitor the bypass operation on President Boris Yeltsin's heart, Interfax news agency said.

The agency said one group of doctors came from Germany and one from the United States -- including Michael DeBakey, the 88-year-old U.S. cardiologist who pioneered the coronary bypass technique more than 30 years ago.
The foreign experts were to watch the operating team of four doctors and eight assistants on a special monitor, the agency added.
Surgery, which is being led by DeBakey's pupil, Russian doctor Renat Akchurin, started at 7 a.m. (0400 GMT).
Interfax said the foreign specialists had timed their arrival to coincide with the most delicate part of the surgery -- working on the open heart.
The operation, a triple or quadruple bypass, is expected to last between six and eight hours and will improve the blood supply to the heart of the 65-year-old Russian president.
